all_found.desc: [BUG] The narrowed failurePatterns no longer match common real failure output the old case-insensitive `failed` caught: dotnet/NUnit 'Failed: 1' and 'Test Run Failed.', '3 test(s) failed', 'go vet failed', 'Failed to compile.', TAP 'not ok', make '*** [test] Error 2'. Verified in a clone at 7431a07: such output next to a 'go test ./... exited 0' line parses as exit 0, so the task-done/pr-ready/epic-ready evidence gates pass over an honest failure report.

[BUG] The stated-failed-check pattern has no negation or zero-count guard: 'no tests failed', '0 tests failed', 'none of the checks failed' match it. Verified: honest passing evidence phrased that way parses as exit 1 and is rejected by the gate — the same false-positive class the bead fixes.
[ADVISORY] The count pattern matches the trailing number in '0 of 10 failed'. Rare phrasing reads as a failure.

[BUG] zeroFailures lets a zero pair with up to two intervening words (digits included) before a failure word, so it strips real failures: '0 passed 3 failed', '0 skipped 3 failed', 'Passed: 0 Failed: 3', '0 failed 3 failed', 'go 1.0 failed', 'exited 0 build failed'. Verified by several lenses: those lines with a success word parse as exit 0 — the fail-closed reader fails open on common runner summaries.

[BUG] Failure shapes missing: Maven/JUnit 'Errors: N' (after 'Failures: 0' is stripped), 'BUILD FAILURE', 'FAILURES!', node:test/TAP '# fail 1', 'ℹ fail 1', bun '1 fail', '2 tests failing', npm 'npm ERR!', MSBuild 'error CS1002:'. Verified: each read as no failure, so a failing run with any success word records passing evidence.

[BUG] zeroFailures accepts a zero preceded by a bare space, so an index label such as 'shard 0 failed', 'worker 0 failed.', 'Job 0 failed' or 'exit code 0 failed' is neutralized as a zero-failure clause. Verified: with a success word those parse as exit 0, hiding a real failure of shard/worker/job 0 from the gates.

[BUG] Upper-case-only FAIL plus count-only lower-case fail drops status-style verdicts: 'Result: Fail', 'Status: Fail', 'lint: fail', '"status":"fail"', 'build fail'. Verified: 'go test ./... ok\nResult: Fail' parses exit 0 — a real failure verdict reads as passing; the base commit read these as failures.

[BUG] The exit-code pattern misses common shapes: 'exit code: 2', 'Process exited with code 1', 'exited with status 3', 'exit=1', 'return code: 1'. Verified: with a success word those read as passing (pre-existing gap, still fail-open).

[BUG] zeroFailures' end delimiter under (?m) does not accept CRLF, and label-then-zero forms ('Failed: 0', 'failed=0', 'FAIL: 0') are not neutralized. Windows-captured or dotnet/ansible passing evidence ('Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 5', 'failed=0') is marked exit 1.

[ADVISORY] The count pattern reads prose like '2 error paths' as a failure; 'fail2ban'/'1 fail-over test' match the fail patterns. Passing evidence mentioning error cases exits 1 (fail-closed false positive).
[ADVISORY] '0 failed in 1s' / '0 failed (cached)' are not neutralized (delimiter required right after the failure word). Fail-closed false positive on some zero summaries.

[BUG] The clause-final N-errors pattern needs punctuation or a line end after the count, so pytest '3 passed, 1 error in 0.12s', mypy 'Found 2 errors in 1 file', clang '1 error generated', 'Interrupted: 1 error during collection' and upper-case pytest 'ERROR tests/x.py - ImportError' lines match no failure pattern. Verified by six lenses: pytest runs with collection/setup errors read as passing evidence (exit 0) and pass the gates.

[BUG] The fail-verdict pattern matches 'fail' ending a test name followed by a duration paren: jest '✓ should fail (3 ms)', go test -v '--- PASS: TestX/fail (0.00s)'. Verified: standard passing verbose output reads as a failure (exit 1) and blocks the gate.

[ADVISORY] Negative or signal exit codes ('exit code: -1', 'exit status -1'), 'rc=1', 'Segmentation fault', 'Killed', Python 'Traceback', Rust 'error[E0308]' are not recognized. With a success word such evidence reads as passing.
[ADVISORY] The zero-label alternative matches inside an error message: 'Error: 0 is not a valid port' is erased. A real error line starting with 0 reads as no failure.

[BUG] The zero-label alternative ends with `[ \t]\w+=`, which consumes the next key and its '=', so in 'failed=0 errors=3' the replacement deletes 'errors=' and leaves a bare 3. Verified: 'tests ok: failed=0 errors=3', 'failures=0 errors=1', 'Failures: 0 exit=1' read as passing (fail-open).

[BUG] An ANSI colour escape directly before FAIL/failed defeats the \b boundary ('m' and 'F' are both word characters). Verified: colourised '\x1b[31mFAIL\x1b[0m' output with a success signal reads as passing.

[BUG] node:test/TAP '# fail 0', 'ℹ fail 0' and bun '0 fail' passing summaries read as failures (the fail+digit and fail-at-line-end rules fire; zeroFailures has no bare 'fail 0' form). Verified: honest passing node:test/TAP/bun evidence is exit 1 and blocks the gates.

[ADVISORY] Residual shapes: bare 'rc' matches release tags (v1.0.0-rc1); indented TAP 'not ok'; 'exited with 1'; 'exit code was 1'; 'TypeError:'/'AssertionError:' (no \b before Error); 'N errors and M warnings'; ctest '0 tests failed out of 5'. Small fail-open or fail-closed gaps in less common shapes.

[BUG] A counted lower-case 'fail' followed by more words ('3 tests fail and 9 pass', 'Tests: 3 fail (of 10)', '1 test fails') is exempted as prose; the base commit's (?i)\bFAIL\b caught it. Verified: with a success signal those parse as exit 0 — a regression against the base commit (fail-open on hand-written counted failures).

[ADVISORY] The fail-verdict patterns count 'fail' followed by '/' or '.', so passing verbose output naming a subtest or file 'fail' ('=== RUN TestX/fail', '✓ src/fail.test.ts') reads as a failure. Fail-closed false positive on some passing verbose output.

[BUG] The 'fail' verdict patterns exempt a fail followed by a word, '(', ' -' or '/' ('Status: Fail because timeout', 'Result: Fail with 3 problems', 'lint: fail (3 warnings)', 'Result: fail - see log', 'build: Fail/timeout', 'RESULT: Fail foo', 'fail (see log)'), although the base commit's (?i)\bFAIL\b read each as a failure. Verified by five lenses running base and head: those lines with a success signal read exit 1 at base and exit 0 at head — a fail-open regression on stated failure verdicts.

[ADVISORY] Smaller regressions against the base: 'exit code\n1' (base \s+ allowed a newline), 'FAIL 0' and 'error: 0' neutralized by the case-insensitive zero label. Rare shapes read as passing that the base read as failing.

[BUG] proseFail is case-insensitive and its modal list includes did/does/do, so an upper-case FAIL verdict before a preposition or after a modal ('FAIL on windows', 'STATUS: FAIL when run with -race', 'will FAIL', jest 'FAIL  before.test.js') and factual reports ('the build did fail', 'does fail on CI', 'Tests fail on CI', 'build fail on step 3') are neutralized. Verified by nine lenses running base 0fa33c2 and head: each reads exit 1 at base and exit 0 at head — a fail-open regression letting stated failures pass the gates.

fix@0.summary: Fail-closed failure reading: (?i)failed and tool shapes count again (plus Failures: N, N failing/failures/errors, exit status, TAP not ok, make Error N, tsc error TS); upper-case FAIL only, so prose 'fail' is exempt; single-line zero-failure reports are stripped first.

fix@1.summary: Bounded zero-failure clause (0/no/none + optional of N or /N + one fixed noun + failure word, delimited, one line) so a zero never swallows a real count; added Errors: N, BUILD FAILURE, FAILURES!, # fail N, N fail, N tests failing, npm ERR!, error CS.

fix@2.summary: Final fail-closed freeform reader: clause-initial zero rule plus zero labels (CRLF, 'in <duration>'), fail verdicts in any case, common exit-code shapes, clause-final N errors; 75-case table.

fix@3.summary: N errors followed by in/during/generated/found; pytest ERROR, Traceback, Segmentation fault, Killed, rustc error[E..]; negative exits and rc=; fail verdict excludes a following paren (test names); zero label must end there.

fix@4.summary: zeroLabel re-emits the following key; ANSI escapes stripped before matching; zeroClause covers fail and 'out of N'; rc needs = or :; indented TAP; exited with N / exit code was N; Error/Exception names, panics; N errors and; go diagnostics and golangci-lint issues.

fix@5.summary: A counted lower-case fail ('3 tests fail', '1 test fails') is a failure; a fail verdict never follows / . - or a word char, so test/path names (TestX/fail, fail.test.ts) are not verdicts. Pre-existing tool-shape gaps filed as a follow-up bead.

fix@6.summary: Base-faithful fail rule (any case, not path/file/compound) with a proseFail neutralizer (modal / preposition) read after countFail; zeroLabel fail lower-case only, errors plural only; exit-code separator allows newlines.

fix@7.summary: proseFail case-sensitive lower-case only, hypothetical/negated modals only, prepositions against/without/before only after a subject word; reportedFail rewrites did/does/do fail to failed; zeroLabel separator optional only for lower-case fail.

findings.issue: zeroFailures accepts a zero preceded by a bare space, so an index label such as 'shard 0 failed', 'worker 0 failed.', 'Job 0 failed' or 'exit code 0 failed' is neutralized as a zero-failure clause.

findings.consequence: Verified: 'go test ./... ok\nResult: Fail' parses exit 0 — a real failure verdict reads as passing; the base commit read these as failures.
findings.issue: Upper-case-only FAIL plus count-only lower-case fail drops status-style verdicts: 'Result: Fail', 'Status: Fail', 'lint: fail', '"status":"fail"', 'build fail'.

findings.consequence: Verified: with a success word those read as passing (pre-existing gap, still fail-open).
findings.issue: The exit-code pattern misses common shapes: 'exit code: 2', 'Process exited with code 1', 'exited with status 3', 'exit=1', 'return code: 1'.

findings.consequence: Windows-captured or dotnet/ansible passing evidence ('Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 5', 'failed=0') is marked exit 1.
findings.issue: zeroFailures' end delimiter under (?m) does not accept CRLF, and label-then-zero forms ('Failed: 0', 'failed=0', 'FAIL: 0') are not neutralized.

findings.consequence: Passing evidence mentioning error cases exits 1 (fail-closed false positive).
findings.issue: The count pattern reads prose like '2 error paths' as a failure; 'fail2ban'/'1 fail-over test' match the fail patterns.

findings.consequence: Fail-closed false positive on some zero summaries.
findings.issue: '0 failed in 1s' / '0 failed (cached)' are not neutralized (delimiter required right after the failure word).

findings.consequence: Verified by six lenses: pytest runs with collection/setup errors read as passing evidence (exit 0) and pass the gates.
findings.issue: The clause-final N-errors pattern needs punctuation or a line end after the count, so pytest '3 passed, 1 error in 0.12s', mypy 'Found 2 errors in 1 file', clang '1 error generated', 'Interrupted: 1 error during collection' and upper-case pytest 'ERROR tests/x.py - ImportError' lines match no failure pattern.

findings.consequence: Verified: standard passing verbose output reads as a failure (exit 1) and blocks the gate.
findings.issue: The fail-verdict pattern matches 'fail' ending a test name followed by a duration paren: jest '✓ should fail (3 ms)', go test -v '--- PASS: TestX/fail (0.00s)'.

findings.consequence: With a success word such evidence reads as passing.
findings.issue: Negative or signal exit codes ('exit code: -1', 'exit status -1'), 'rc=1', 'Segmentation fault', 'Killed', Python 'Traceback', Rust 'error[E0308]' are not recognized.

findings.consequence: A real error line starting with 0 reads as no failure.
findings.issue: The zero-label alternative matches inside an error message: 'Error: 0 is not a valid port' is erased.

findings.consequence: Verified: 'tests ok: failed=0 errors=3', 'failures=0 errors=1', 'Failures: 0 exit=1' read as passing (fail-open).
findings.issue: The zero-label alternative ends with `[ \t]\w+=`, which consumes the next key and its '=', so in 'failed=0 errors=3' the replacement deletes 'errors=' and leaves a bare 3.

findings.consequence: Verified: colourised '\x1b[31mFAIL\x1b[0m' output with a success signal reads as passing.
findings.issue: An ANSI colour escape directly before FAIL/failed defeats the \b boundary ('m' and 'F' are both word characters).

findings.consequence: Verified: honest passing node:test/TAP/bun evidence is exit 1 and blocks the gates.
findings.issue: node:test/TAP '# fail 0', 'ℹ fail 0' and bun '0 fail' passing summaries read as failures (the fail+digit and fail-at-line-end rules fire; zeroFailures has no bare 'fail 0' form).

findings.consequence: Small fail-open or fail-closed gaps in less common shapes.
findings.issue: Residual shapes: bare 'rc' matches release tags (v1.0.0-rc1); indented TAP 'not ok'; 'exited with 1'; 'exit code was 1'; 'TypeError:'/'AssertionError:' (no \b before Error); 'N errors and M warnings'; ctest '0 tests failed out of 5'.

findings.consequence: Verified: with a success signal those parse as exit 0 — a regression against the base commit (fail-open on hand-written counted failures).
findings.issue: A counted lower-case 'fail' followed by more words ('3 tests fail and 9 pass', 'Tests: 3 fail (of 10)', '1 test fails') is exempted as prose; the base commit's (?i)\bFAIL\b caught it.

findings.consequence: Pre-existing fail-open gaps on those shapes (not regressions of this diff); follow-up bead.
findings.issue: Tool shapes neither the base commit nor this change recognise: JSON '"exitCode": 1', jest coverage-threshold 'not met', pytest 'no tests ran', jest 'No tests found', eslint 'too many warnings', make 'No rule to make target', 'Aborted (core dumped)', Go 'panic:', 'command not found', 'timed out', 'N errored/crashed', 'Failure:' headers.

findings.consequence: Fail-closed false positive on some passing verbose output.
findings.issue: The fail-verdict patterns count 'fail' followed by '/' or '.', so passing verbose output naming a subtest or file 'fail' ('=== RUN TestX/fail', '✓ src/fail.test.ts') reads as a failure.

findings.consequence: A regression producing no receipt panics without naming the case.
findings.issue: The table indexes Receipts[0] without a length check.

findings.consequence: Verified by five lenses running base and head: those lines with a success signal read exit 1 at base and exit 0 at head — a fail-open regression on stated failure verdicts.
findings.issue: The 'fail' verdict patterns exempt a fail followed by a word, '(', ' -' or '/' ('Status: Fail because timeout', 'Result: Fail with 3 problems', 'lint: fail (3 warnings)', 'Result: fail - see log', 'build: Fail/timeout', 'RESULT: Fail foo', 'fail (see log)'), although the base commit's (?i)\bFAIL\b read each as a failure.

findings.consequence: Rare shapes read as passing that the base read as failing.
findings.issue: Smaller regressions against the base: 'exit code\n1' (base \s+ allowed a newline), 'FAIL 0' and 'error: 0' neutralized by the case-insensitive zero label.

findings.consequence: Verified by nine lenses running base 0fa33c2 and head: each reads exit 1 at base and exit 0 at head — a fail-open regression letting stated failures pass the gates.
findings.issue: proseFail is case-insensitive and its modal list includes did/does/do, so an upper-case FAIL verdict before a preposition or after a modal ('FAIL on windows', 'STATUS: FAIL when run with -race', 'will FAIL', jest 'FAIL  before.test.js') and factual reports ('the build did fail', 'does fail on CI', 'Tests fail on CI', 'build fail on step 3') are neutralized.

findings.consequence: Rare shapes read as passing.
findings.issue: zeroLabel's optional separator erases 'Build failed 0' and 'FAILED 0', which the base read as failures.

findings.consequence: Verified by running base and head: those read exit 1 at base and exit 0 at head — a fail-open regression.
findings.issue: proseFail's modal branch includes bare 'to', so failure reports 'continues to fail', 'started to fail', 'seems to fail', 'going to fail' are neutralized; 'still fail before 5s timeout' slips through the 'before' preposition.

findings.consequence: Maintainers can misread the exemption set and the ordering invariants (countFail and reportedFail before proseFail).
findings.issue: The failurePatterns header comment still describes the pre-proseFail design, and the ARCHITECTURE 'Exempt (mr-r3y)' sentence runs the zero exemptions into the 'never' conditions.
